text:
Liam: Quick question — I was promoted and my medical coverage tier moved from employee-only to family with an effective date of 2023-08-15. Our HSA employer contribution is normally a monthly deposit. Will the company prorate the employer HSA contribution for August or does the new amount only start on 9/1? Also, I turn 55 this month — does that change anything automatically for catch-up HSA contributions?

Aisha (People Ops): congrats! 🎉 good q. two parts — coverage tier change proration and 55+ catch-up. can you confirm the promotion effective date (you wrote 8/15) and whether payroll already ran for the mid-aug pay? if you'd rather DM the exact dates/paycheck, that works.

Liam: thanks! payroll hasn't run for the pay period with the 8/15 date yet (next run is 8/22). happy to DM with exact paycheck date.

Benefits Bot: FYI — our benefits handbook article on HSA employer deposits: https://handbook.redwood/inbox/benefits/hsa-deposits (see section "Employer deposit timing").

Priya - Benefits: TL;DR: employer HSA contributions are determined by coverage tier on the 1st of the month. That means a mid-month switch effective 8/15 will change the deposit amount starting in September's employer deposit. We do not automatically prorate the employer contribution for the partial month.

Priya - Benefits: On the 55+ catch-up — catch-up contribution is an employee election. Payroll can start deducting the additional $1,000/month (or annual catch-up amount prorated across remaining pay periods) once you submit an updated pre-tax election. We do not automatically enable catch-up based solely on age; employee action is required.

Priya - Benefits: If you want any retroactive off-cycle employer deposit (i.e., company covers the difference for August), that's handled by Payroll as an exception and is not standard. It may be possible within 30 days of the effective date but requires a payroll ticket and manager approval. There can be a small processing fee for off-cycle runs.

Priya - Benefits: To request payroll review, please open a ticket using this template (copy/paste into the Payroll queue):

```
Subject: Off-cycle HSA employer deposit request — Liam — effective 2023-08-15
Employee: Liam (email: liam@redwood.example)
Requested action: Apply prorated employer HSA top-up for Aug or confirm no retroactive deposit
Effective date: 2023-08-15
Payroll run affected: 2023-08-22
Manager approval: attached (yes/no)
Reason: promotion/coverage tier change mid-month
```

Priya - Benefits: If you only want to start the 55+ catch-up, submit the pre-tax election change in Workday and mention the effective pay date; Payroll will pick it up in the next standard run.

Liam: got it — thanks @Priya and @Aisha. i'll DM the exact payroll run info and open the payroll ticket if manager signs off. appreciate the clarity. :thumbsup:

Aisha (People Ops): thanks! if you want, i can loop in your manager on the ticket request to speed approval.

Priya - Benefits: happy to help — ping here once you have the ticket number and i'll monitor.

Liam: will do. thanks everyone!
